Application Materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload to your application clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents (not copies or certified copies). These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. A reference provided by email must be sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as “Yahoo” or “Hotmail” are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof.
You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **UK degree requirements:** A **2:1 or above** at undergraduate level in **actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, econometrics, mathematical economics, finance, or engineering**.
- **Other routes:** Applicants with a good **2:2 degree (55% or above)** will be considered on an individual basis. Other education backgrounds can be considered subject to demonstrating satisfactory knowledge of **actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, finance or engineering**.
- **China applicants:** Queen Mary normally considers a **Bachelor Degree (minimum 4 years) from selected institutions** for entry to postgraduate taught programmes. For Chinese qualifications: **UK 1st class degree: 85 to 95%**; **UK 2:1 degree: 70 to 80%**; **UK 2:2 degree: 65 to 75%**. Offer conditions will vary depending on the institution you are applying from.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English Language requirements for entry to postgraduate taught and research programmes in the School of Mathematics falls within the following English band: **Band 4:** IELTS (Academic) minimum score **6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking**.
We accept a range of English tests and qualifications categorised in our English bands for you to demonstrate your level of English Language proficiency. See [all accepted English tests](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/) that we deem equivalent to these IELTS scores.

Program Overview.content:
The role of a traditional actuary is changing. Organisations require actuarial professionals with the analytical and statistical skills needed to analyse the large sets of data that they are being presented in today’s data-driven world. You should study this programme if you are seeking to pursue or further your actuarial professional qualification, while at the same time future-proofing your skills.
If you have prior training in actuarial science, to obtain an Associate level qualification from the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (IFoA), you will need to pass the Core Practices (CP1, CP2, CP3) examination subjects after completing the Core Principles. If you have already passed or achieved exemption from the Core Principles, you can jump straight into studying modules consistent with the Core Practices, which are at the heart of this programme. If you have not studied actuarial science before, there is also the option to include selected Core Principles in the MSc programme.
- You will be taught by faculty members who are Fellows and Independent Examiners with the IFoA.
- The actuarial training has a mixture of theory and professional practice.
- You will be taught the skills needed to become highly employable across a wide range of industries.
After successful completion of the course, students should have the skills necessary to obtain employment in a wide variety of roles in the field of general or life insurance, pension funds, healthcare, banking, regulatory bodies, or broadly in consultancy and other corporations or public organisations.
The compulsory component of the programme includes actuarial risk management, machine learning, time series for business, and a dissertation project consistent with Modelling Practice, CP2 and Communication Practice, CP3 of the IFoA syllabus. In addition, students choose from a range of modules covering both Data Science and Actuarial Science, depending on their interests and previous background.

Curriculum.content:
The Actuarial Science and Data Analytics MSc is offered on campus at Queen Mary London Campuses, with a full-time September offering lasting 12 months and a part-time September offering lasting 24 months.
The programme consists of **180 credits**: **120 credits** of core, compulsory and guided elective taught modules, plus a **60-credit dissertation/project**. It consists of four compulsory taught modules, four elective modules, and a summer dissertation project. Full-time students are expected to complete eight taught modules and the project dissertation in one academic year.
- Semester A compulsory modules: MTH7013P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 1 (CP1); MTH786P [7] Machine Learning with Python.
- Semester A electives: MTH7025P [7] Survival Models (CS2); MTH7026P [7] Foundations of Mathematics and Statistics for Actuaries (CS2); MTH765P [7] Storing, Manipulating and Visualising Data; MTH739P [7] Topics in Scientific Computing.
- Semester B compulsory modules: MTH7014P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 2 (CP1); MTH783P [7] Time Series for Business (CS2).
- Semester B electives: MTH7027P [7] Financial Engineering (CM2); MTH7028P [7] Mathematical Tools for Asset and Liability Management (CM2); MTH793P [7] Advanced Machine Learning; MTH792P [7] Financial Data Analytics; MTH767P [7] Neural Networks and Deep Learning; MTH791P [7] Computational Statistics with R.
- Semester C core: Actuarial Science and Data Analytics Dissertation (CP2 and CP3), **60 credits**.
Part-time diet:
- Semester A, Year 1 compulsory: MTH7013P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 1 (CP1); MTH786P [7] Machine Learning with Python.
- Semester B, Year 1 compulsory: MTH7014P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 2 (CP1); MTH783P [7] Time Series for Business (CS2).
- Semester A, Year 2 electives, choose 2: MTH7025P [7] Survival Models (CS2); MTH7026P [7] Foundations of Mathematics and Statistics (CS2); MTH765P [7] Storing, Manipulating and Visualising Data; MTH739P [7] Topics in Scientific Computing.
- Semester B, Year 2 electives, choose 2: MTH7027P [7] Financial Engineering (CM2); MTH7028P [7] Mathematical Tools for Asset and Liability Management (CM2); MTH793P [7] Advanced Machine Learning; MTH792P [7] Financial Data Analytics; MTH767P [7] Neural Networks and Deep Learning; MTH791P [7] Computational Statistics with R.
- Semester C, Year 2 core: MTH7029P [7] Actuarial Science and Data Analytics Dissertation (CP2 and CP3), **60 credits**.
Students choose elective modules according to their academic background and interests, in consultation with the Programme Director and other staff as needed. Students with no prior accreditation and QM students with an undergraduate degree from SMS without the modules that cover CS2 and CM2 can choose the elective modules covering CS2 and CM2. If a student already has accreditations for either CS2 or CM2, or graduated from QM SMS with an undergraduate degree with modules covering CS2 or CM2, their choice of electives on this MSc will exclude CM2 or CS2 modules.
The MSc dissertation project is a summer dissertation project and a significant component of assessment. Students conduct independent research, design and execute a research study, analyze data, and present findings in a formal written dissertation. The project consists of two parts: modelling and communication, focusing on critical analysis and modelling of common actuarial data using analytical and statistical methods, and effective written communication of research and actuarial/financial solutions to actuarial and non-actuarial audiences.

Financial Aid.content: Queen Mary is pleased to offer a number of generous scholarships to students on our MSc programmes. A wide range of other scholarships and bursaries are available, including the [Queen Mary Alumni Loyalty Award](http://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/queen-mary-alumni-loyalty-award/) and the UK government's international [Chevening Awards](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/chevening-awards.html). **Find out about all scholarships and bursaries available to Queen Mary postgraduate applicants [here](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/).** If you have any questions about Scholarships available to applicants within the School of Mathematical Sciences, please contact [maths@qmul.ac.uk](mailto:maths@qmul.ac.uk).

Multiple Applications.content: You may apply for a **maximum of two taught programmes** or **one taught and one research programme** at Queen Mary per application cycle. You can only study for one qualification at a time, so if you receive offers for both programmes you will be required to accept one and decline the other. The university does **not** charge an application fee.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: The withdrawal and deferral process differs depending on your programme level and your enrolment status. However, if you were accepted through Clearing then you cannot defer and will need to decline your offer and apply via the main application cycle. Please consider the deferral deadlines which are published online for [Postgraduate Taught](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/deadlines/) programmes. You can refer to our [Enrolment FAQs](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/newstudents/faqs/enrolment/) which set out in more detail the withdrawal and deferral processes.
